summary: Local MQTT tooling for people and AI agents.
roleSummary: Python core, desktop UI & MCP integration
contribution: Built a local MQTT developer tool with a desktop interface, persistent observations, and an MCP interface for agents.

decisions.title: Keep state and credentials local
decisions.reason: SQLite stores observed state; the operating system keyring holds broker credentials. Inspection does not require a hosted service.

decisions.title: Separate inspection from control
decisions.reason: MCP access is read-only by default. Publishing can affect physical devices, so control requires an explicit opt-in.

decisions.title: Make observation limits visible
decisions.reason: Freshness and health metadata put payloads in context. Stored observations describe what TopicGate has seen, rather than claiming to be complete broker history.

lesson: Published on PyPI and listed in the MCP Registry. The engineering focus is a clear boundary between observed data, its freshness, and actions that change a device.

architecture.description: MQTT messages enter a local observation layer backed by SQLite. The desktop and MCP interfaces expose this state; broker credentials stay in the system keyring. Device control is opt-in.
architecture.source:
flowchart LR
        broker[MQTT broker] -->|messages| core[Local observation layer]
        core <--> store[(SQLite observations)]
        keys[System keyring] -. credentials .-> core
        core --> desktop[Desktop observer]
        core --> mcp[Read-only MCP]
        mcp --> agents[AI agents]
        control[Opt-in control] -->|publish| broker

coreStory: I started TopicGate while working on SmartHomeBridge: I needed a better way to observe MQTT topics and diagnose what was happening. An MCP server would let agents help with that work, so I built both an MCP interface and a desktop app.

I developed it incrementally, starting with subscriptions, then adding broker profiles, health observations and history. Credentials and stored observations stay on the user's machine; MCP shares requested observations with the connected agent, and device control is explicitly opt-in.
